You are going to turn a workout into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme workout and deliver a live timeline: Partner Upper-Body Superset Session for 2 lifters
Resource limits: one bench and barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar, two ergs, about 25 minutes.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Partner Upper-Body Superset Session

Two lifters, one flat bench with a barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar and two rowing ergs. The whole session should take about 25 minutes. You work as a pair: while Partner A is on the first exercise of a superset, Partner B is on the second, and then you swap; nobody waits for equipment if you keep the order.

Warm-up
Both partners start together with 5 minutes of easy rowing on the ergs, followed by 3 minutes of arm circles and band pull-aparts.

Superset A: bench press and dumbbell row (2 rounds)
Partner A loads the bar and does a set of 8 bench presses, which takes about 40 seconds. Partner B starts on the dumbbell row at the same time, 8 per side, also about 40 seconds. Then swap: A goes to the rows once B has finished with the dumbbells, and B takes the bench as soon as A racks the bar. After both exercises, rest 90 seconds before the next round. Do 2 rounds, resting after each.

Superset B: overhead press and pull-ups (2 rounds)
Move straight on after the last rest. Partner A does 8 strict overhead presses with the dumbbells, about 45 seconds, while Partner B does a set of pull-ups, 6 to 10 reps, about 30 seconds. Swap when both are done: A moves to the pull-up bar, and B takes the dumbbells when A sets them down. Rest 2 minutes between rounds; there is no rest after the second round.

Cool-down
Finish together with 5 minutes of stretching: doorway chest stretch, lat stretch on the pull-up bar, and slow shoulder rolls.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. ```

This is a partner upper-body superset workout for exactly two lifters, designed to run as a single live-timed session lasting roughly 25 minutes total, with no fixed finish clock time given — the instruction is to end as early as the work naturally allows. The equipment is scarce and shared: one flat bench with barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar, and two rowing ergs (enough for both partners to row simultaneously). The two lifters move through the session as a synchronized pair: they start together on the ergs for a 5-minute warm-up row, then together for 3 minutes of arm circles/band pull-aparts, then into Superset A (bench press / dumbbell row, 2 rounds, each exercise ~40s, with the partners swapping stations once both finish their set, followed by a 90s rest after each round), then directly into Superset B (overhead press / pull-ups, 2 rounds, ~45s and ~30s respectively, swapping stations similarly, with a 2-minute rest between rounds but no rest after the final round), and finally together again for a 5-minute cool-down stretch. The binding constraints are: single-use equipment (one bench/barbell, one dumbbell pair, one pull-up bar) that must alternate between the two partners within each superset round without either person waiting idle, two ergs so warm-up rowing can be simultaneous, exactly 2 actors, and specific rest/hold periods (90s and 120s) that must elapse before the next round begins. Nothing in the source appears truncated — all sections (warm-up, both supersets, cool-down) are present and complete.

A **track** represents one continuous, sequential thread of work for a single "doer" (or a single piece of equipment's timeline) — its steps run one after another with no overlap, so anything happening concurrently with that thread (a different person, a different exercise) has to live in its own track. Each **step** carries exactly one duration shape: `fixed` seconds, a `variable` min/max/default range, or `indefinite` (ended manually by the person doing it). A **startTrigger** is how a step is anchored to time or to another step's completion — `programStart` for t=0, `programStartOffset` for a flat delay, `afterStep`/`afterStepWithBuffer` to chain off a prior step (optionally per-instance with `instances`), `manual` for a user tap, `onAbort` for a fallback, and `compound` to wait on several triggers at once. `stepId` values must be unique across the entire program, not just within a track, since triggers reference them globally. Any step that occupies a piece of shared, single-instance (or limited-capacity) equipment declares a `task`, and that `task` must have a corresponding `resourceConstraints` entry whose `maxConcurrent` is the actual enforcement mechanism — e.g. one bench means `maxConcurrent: 1`, two ergs means `maxConcurrent: 2`. Repeated work (n reps of the same structural step, like n rounds of a superset) should be expressed with `replicates` on a single step rather than duplicated steps, chaining follow-on work with `instances: "each"` or waiting for the full set with `instances: "all"`, and using `maxInFlight` if a holding area caps how many can be "in progress" at once — though for this two-round superset session, the rounds differ enough (rest timing, swap logic) that I'm currently leaning toward writing them as sequential steps in each partner's track rather than `replicates`, since each round's swap already threads through both partners' tracks rather than a shared holding buffer.

For this workout I expect two tracks (Partner A, Partner B), each moving through warm-up → superset A rounds → superset B rounds → cool-down, synchronized at the group phases and offset/staggered during the swaps within each superset.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else.
